title: Oracle LISTAGG DISTINCT: Remove Duplicates (With Examples)
description: Remove duplicate values from Oracle LISTAGG with DISTINCT in 19c, or a subquery on 11g to 18c. Includes output, ordering tips and an ORA-01489 fix.

sources.title: Oracle Database 19c SQL Language Reference: LISTAGG
Oracle Database 19c SQL Language Reference: Aggregate Functions
Oracle by Example (19c): Avoid Errors due to Values Generated by the LISTAGG Function

reviewNotes: Examples written from the Oracle 19c SQL Language Reference; none were run, so all queries and outputs need a test run on 19c (and Method 2 on an 18c or older instance if available). Check: (1) the exact truncated-output format for ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE ... WITH COUNT (spacing before the count); the '(12)' value is illustrative only. (2) The SQL reference says WITH COUNT is the default, while the Oracle by Example LISTAGG tutorial says WITHOUT COUNT is; the article follows the SQL reference, please confirm. (3) The error raised by LISTAGG DISTINCT on 18c was not verified, so the article only says it is 'rejected'. (4) WM_CONCAT statement (not available from 12c) is from general knowledge, not a fetched doc. (5) I avoided LISTAGG(DISTINCT x) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY other_col) and DISTINCT with the analytic OVER clause because the docs do not spell out their behaviour.

data.text: To remove duplicates from LISTAGG in Oracle 19c and later, put DISTINCT inside the function: LISTAGG(DISTINCT product_name, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name). Oracle drops repeated values first and then joins what is left into one string. On 18c, 12c and 11g the keyword is not available, so you remove the duplicates in a subquery before calling LISTAGG.

This tutorial shows both methods on a small orders table, with the output of every query. It also covers the problems you hit next: values that differ only in case or spaces, ordering the list by a different column, and the ORA-01489 error when the list grows too long.
How LISTAGG works

LISTAGG is an aggregate function. For each group of rows it sorts the values using the ORDER BY inside WITHIN GROUP, then concatenates them into a single VARCHAR2 string with the delimiter you choose between them. One group in, one string out.

By default it keeps every value, so if a customer bought the same product three times, the product appears three times. That is the same as ALL, which the documentation describes as optional and "provided for semantic clarity". Adding DISTINCT tells Oracle to keep each value once. NULL values are ignored either way, just like in SUM or COUNT(column).
The full syntax in Oracle 19c looks like this:

data.code:
LISTAGG( [ALL | DISTINCT] measure_expr [, 'delimiter']
         [ON OVERFLOW ERROR
          | ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE ['indicator'] [WITH | WITHOUT COUNT]] )
  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY sort_expr)
  [OVER (PARTITION BY ...)]
data.caption: LISTAGG syntax (Oracle 19c)

content: Controls what happens when the result is too long
Sets the order of values in the list

data.text: Sample setup
Create a small orders table and add a few rows. Some customers ordered the same product more than once, and one order has no product name, so you can see how duplicates and NULLs behave.

data.caption: Create and fill the orders table

data.text: The problem: LISTAGG repeats values
Start with a plain LISTAGG that lists the products each customer has ordered:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       LISTAGG(product_name, ', ')
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name) AS products
  FROM orders
 GROUP BY customer_name
 ORDER BY customer_name;
data.caption: Plain LISTAGG keeps duplicates

data.code:
CUSTOMER_NAME  PRODUCTS
-------------  ---------------------------------
Asha           Keyboard, Laptop, Laptop, Mouse
Meena          Mouse
Ravi           Cable, Monitor, Monitor
data.caption: Output (expected output)

data.text: Asha bought a laptop twice, so Laptop appears twice. Ravi's Monitor is repeated too. Meena's second order has a NULL product, and LISTAGG skipped it without adding an empty entry or an extra comma. For a report that should answer "which products does this customer buy", the repeats are noise.
Method 1: LISTAGG DISTINCT (Oracle 19c and later)
Add DISTINCT as the first word inside the brackets:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       LISTAGG(DISTINCT product_name, ', ')
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name) AS products
  FROM orders
 GROUP BY customer_name
 ORDER BY customer_name;
data.caption: Remove duplicates with DISTINCT

data.code:
CUSTOMER_NAME  PRODUCTS
-------------  -------------------------
Asha           Keyboard, Laptop, Mouse
Meena          Mouse
Ravi           Cable, Monitor
data.caption: Output (expected output)

data.text: Each product now appears once per customer. Oracle removes duplicates within each group, not across the whole table, so Mouse still appears for both Asha and Meena. That is what you want: the GROUP BY decides the groups, and DISTINCT works inside each one.
Show the count next to the list
A common report shows how many orders a customer placed and how many different products that covers. Combine LISTAGG(DISTINCT ...) with COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT ...):

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       COUNT(*)                     AS order_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT product_name) AS product_count,
       LISTAGG(DISTINCT product_name, ', ')
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name) AS products
  FROM orders
 GROUP BY customer_name
 ORDER BY customer_name;
data.caption: Counts and the distinct list together

data.code:
CUSTOMER_NAME  ORDER_COUNT  PRODUCT_COUNT  PRODUCTS
-------------  -----------  -------------  -----------------------
Asha                     4              3  Keyboard, Laptop, Mouse
Meena                    2              1  Mouse
Ravi                     3              2  Cable, Monitor
data.caption: Output (expected output)

data.text: Meena has 2 orders but only 1 product, because COUNT(*) counts the row with the NULL product while COUNT(DISTINCT product_name) and LISTAGG both ignore it. The product count always matches the number of items in the list, which is a handy sanity check.
Method 2: remove duplicates in a subquery (11g, 12c, 18c)
If your database is older than 19c, LISTAGG(DISTINCT ...) is rejected. Make the rows unique first, then aggregate:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       LISTAGG(product_name, ', ')
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name) AS products
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT customer_name, product_name
          FROM orders)
 GROUP BY customer_name
 ORDER BY customer_name;
data.caption: Works on every version that has LISTAGG

data.code:
CUSTOMER_NAME  PRODUCTS
-------------  -------------------------
Asha           Keyboard, Laptop, Mouse
Meena          Mouse
Ravi           Cable, Monitor
data.caption: Output (expected output)

data.text: The result is the same as Method 1. The inner query returns one row per customer and product pair, so there is nothing left to repeat. The key point is that the inner SELECT DISTINCT must list exactly the grouping column and the column you aggregate. If you add order_id or order_date to it, every row becomes unique again and the duplicates come back.

If the same query also needs other aggregates over all rows, such as COUNT(*) or SUM(amount), the subquery method changes them too, because it throws rows away. In that case either upgrade the LISTAGG part to 19c DISTINCT, or compute the list in a separate subquery and join it back.
Order the distinct list by a different column

Sometimes you want each product once, but in the order the customer first bought it, not alphabetically. Do the de-duplication with GROUP BY so you can keep the first order date, then sort the list by that date:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       LISTAGG(product_name, ', ')
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY first_ordered, product_name) AS products
  FROM (SELECT customer_name,
               product_name,
               MIN(order_date) AS first_ordered
          FROM orders
         WHERE product_name IS NOT NULL
         GROUP BY customer_name, product_name)
 GROUP BY customer_name
 ORDER BY customer_name;
data.caption: Each product once, in order of first purchase

data.code:
CUSTOMER_NAME  PRODUCTS
-------------  -------------------------
Asha           Laptop, Mouse, Keyboard
Meena          Mouse
Ravi           Monitor, Cable
data.caption: Output (expected output)

data.text: Asha bought the laptop on 5 January, the mouse on 6 January and the keyboard on 11 February, so the list follows that order. The second sort key, product_name, breaks ties when two products were first bought on the same day. The Oracle documentation notes that LISTAGG is deterministic only if the ORDER BY list gives a unique ordering, so a tie-breaker keeps the output stable from run to run.
This pattern works on every version and is the clearest way to express "distinct, but sorted by something else". On 19c you can still use it whenever the sort key is not the value you are listing.
Handle ORA-01489 when the list is too long
LISTAGG returns a VARCHAR2, so its result has a size limit. When the joined string goes over it, the query fails:

data.code: ORA-01489: result of string concatenation is too long
data.caption: Output (expected output)

data.text: The limit depends on the MAX_STRING_SIZE initialization parameter. With the default, STANDARD, the limit is 4000 bytes. With EXTENDED it is 32767 bytes. Bytes, not characters: in an AL32UTF8 database, non-English text such as Hindi or Tamil uses more than one byte per character, so you reach the limit sooner.

data.caption: Check the current setting (SQL*Plus or SQLcl)

data.text: Truncate instead of failing
From Oracle 12.2 you can ask LISTAGG to cut the list short instead of raising the error. The overflow clause goes after the delimiter, inside the brackets, and works together with DISTINCT:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       LISTAGG(DISTINCT product_name, ', '
               ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE '...' WITH COUNT)
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name) AS products
  FROM orders
 GROUP BY customer_name
 ORDER BY customer_name;
data.caption: DISTINCT with overflow protection

data.text: With our small table nothing overflows, so the output is the same as Method 1. When a list does overflow, Oracle keeps as many whole values as fit (it never cuts a value in half), then adds the delimiter, the truncation indicator and, with WITH COUNT, the number of values it left out in brackets. A truncated row ends like this:

Here 12 would be the number of values that did not fit. According to the SQL reference, if you leave out both WITH COUNT and WITHOUT COUNT, the default is WITH COUNT, and the default indicator is .... ON OVERFLOW ERROR is the default overflow behaviour and gives you the ORA-01489 error above.
DISTINCT also helps with overflow, because duplicates are removed before Oracle checks the length. A list that failed with repeats may fit once they are gone.

Changing MAX_STRING_SIZE to EXTENDED is a one-way change. It needs the database (or PDB) opened in UPGRADE mode and the utl32k.sql script, and you cannot go back to STANDARD. It is a DBA decision, not a quick fix for one report. Try ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE first.
Common mistakes
Values that look the same but are not

DISTINCT compares the exact values. With the default binary comparison, Mouse, mouse and Mouse (with a trailing space) in VARCHAR2 columns are three different values, and all three appear in the list. Clean the value inside the function:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       LISTAGG(DISTINCT INITCAP(TRIM(product_name)), ', ')
         WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY INITCAP(TRIM(product_name))) AS products
  FROM orders
 GROUP BY customer_name;
data.caption: Normalise case and spaces before removing duplicates

data.text: Use the same expression in the ORDER BY so the sort matches what you display. If messy values are common, fix them in the data instead of in every query.
Forgetting the delimiter
The delimiter defaults to NULL, not a comma. LISTAGG(DISTINCT product_name) for Asha returns KeyboardLaptopMouse. Always pass the separator you want as the second argument.
Leaving out GROUP BY

If you select customer_name next to LISTAGG and forget GROUP BY customer_name, Oracle raises ORA-00937: not a single-group group function. Every non-aggregated column in the SELECT list must be in the GROUP BY.
Adding extra columns to the de-duplication subquery
In Method 2, SELECT DISTINCT customer_name, product_name, order_date keeps Asha's two laptop orders, because their dates differ. Select only the columns that define a duplicate.
Using LISTAGG DISTINCT on 18c or earlier

Code written on a 19c development database can fail on an older production database. Check the version with SELECT banner FROM v$version; before you rely on DISTINCT, or use the subquery method if the code must run on both.
Performance tips

items.content: Filter first. A WHERE clause that reduces the rows before grouping means less sorting for both GROUP BY and DISTINCT.

DISTINCT and WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) both need the values in each group sorted. On large tables watch for big sort operations in the execution plan, and give the session enough PGA memory for the sort.
Keep lists short and for display. A comma-separated list of thousands of values is hard to read and close to the length limit. If an application needs the individual values, return them as rows.

Do not store LISTAGG output in a table column to query later. Searching inside a comma-separated string cannot use a normal index on the values. Keep the detail rows and build the list when you read it.

data.text: Frequently asked questions
How do I remove duplicates in LISTAGG in Oracle?

On Oracle 19c and later, write LISTAGG(DISTINCT column, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY column). On earlier versions, select the distinct grouping and value columns in a subquery and run LISTAGG on that subquery.
Which Oracle version supports LISTAGG DISTINCT?
Oracle Database 19c added DISTINCT to LISTAGG. LISTAGG itself arrived in 11g Release 2, and the ON OVERFLOW clause in 12c Release 2.
What is the maximum length of a LISTAGG result?
4000 bytes when MAX_STRING_SIZE = STANDARD (the default) and 32767 bytes when it is EXTENDED. Going over the limit raises ORA-01489 unless you use ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE.
Can I use WM_CONCAT instead of LISTAGG?
No. WM_CONCAT was an undocumented, unsupported function and it is not available from Oracle 12c. Replace it with LISTAGG.
What is the PostgreSQL equivalent of LISTAGG DISTINCT?
PostgreSQL uses string_agg, with the DISTINCT and ORDER BY inside the brackets:

data.code:
SELECT customer_name,
       string_agg(DISTINCT product_name, ', ' ORDER BY product_name) AS products
  FROM orders
 GROUP BY customer_name;
data.caption: PostgreSQL version of the same query

data.text: In PostgreSQL, when you use DISTINCT, the ORDER BY expressions must appear in the argument list, so you can only sort by the value itself.
Summary

items.content: Use LISTAGG(DISTINCT col, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col) on Oracle 19c and later.
On 11g to 18c, de-duplicate in a subquery that selects only the grouping column and the listed column.
To list each value once but sort by another column, GROUP BY the value with MIN() of the sort column, then LISTAGG.
Clean case and spaces with TRIM and UPPER or INITCAP inside the function when the data is messy.
Always pass a delimiter, and add a tie-breaker to the ORDER BY for stable output.
Prevent ORA-01489 with ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE (12.2 and later) before considering MAX_STRING_SIZE = EXTENDED.

linkedin.post:
Your LISTAGG report shows "Laptop, Laptop, Mouse". Here is how to list each value only once in Oracle.

1. Oracle 19c and later: put DISTINCT inside the function.
LISTAGG(DISTINCT product_name, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY product_name)

2. On 11g, 12c or 18c: run SELECT DISTINCT customer_name, product_name in a subquery first, then LISTAGG on top. Add no other columns, or the duplicates come back.

3. Want each value once but sorted by first purchase date? GROUP BY the value with MIN(order_date), then sort the LISTAGG by that date.

4. "Mouse" and "mouse " are different values to DISTINCT. Use TRIM and INITCAP inside the function if your data is messy.

5. ORA-01489 means the list passed 4000 bytes (or 32767 with MAX_STRING_SIZE = EXTENDED). From 12.2, ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE '...' WITH COUNT cuts the list instead of failing.
